correctness.rationale: The unit ball is exactly a rectangular fiber system because each leaf-pair Lipschitz constraint follows from two hub inequalities. All active leaf-center inequalities with rho_i<2 admit uniquely active witnesses, proving the facet list. A vertex must select every leaf fiber endpoint and have its hub coordinate pinned by a cube bound or a double-active clipping event; the converse follows from m+1 independent active equations. Counting is exact because each leaf interval has two distinct endpoints, and generic maximality follows by union bounding 2k elementary anchoring events. The dual formula follows from independent leaf maximizations and piecewise-linear concavity; sorting breakpoint slope jumps gives O(m log m). The reproducibility program independently checked the candidate set against all active-set intersections for 13 length vectors, facet witnesses, and all three dual methods, reporting 897 exact-rational assertions. These checks are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new theorem gives a complete vertex/facet phase classification for every positive weighted star, including collision counts, and a closed finite-breakpoint signed-measure dual norm in O(m log m) arithmetic. Hille–Theewis 2022 proves general computational reductions but says explicit multi-Dirac formulas are not available at the corresponding level (Section 4); Hille–Theewis 2023 supplies general norming constructions rather than these counts. Gordon–Petrov requires generic strict metrics, violated by the augmented weighted-star metric whenever there are at least two leaves. The older Farmer intrinsic characterization may imply a qualitative criterion but not the explicit count and algorithm on its face; full text could not be examined. Search failure is not claimed as proof of absolute novelty.

value.rationale: The invariant is the full face structure of the standard bounded Lipschitz/FM unit ball on an arbitrary weighted star, with no arbitrary metric slice. The generic maximum (m+2)2^m, exact collision-loss rule, and linear facet count quantify a natural class with permanent triangle equalities that falls outside generic-strict Lipschitz-polytope theory. Exact O(m log m) support-function evaluation for arbitrary signed masses is directly motivated by finite-measure norm computation and genuinely stronger as an explicit result than a general finite-dimensional optimization formulation. The entire family and degeneracy thresholds are classified, rather than adding a small isolated example.
